name: #MeToo

We will be working with the Title IX Office for reform, and providing survivors with the opportunity to access legal help throughout the Title IX process.

The office seeks to engage and inspire faculty and staff by providing opportunities for growth and recognition.

description: The Academic Integrity Board is a diverse group of students, faculty, and administrators who are committed to promoting academic integrity and raising the awareness of integrity issues at Case Western Reserve University. The Board conducts programs for both students and faculty that encourage discussion about issues about academic integrity and related issues. This is an all inclusive club so anyone and everyone is welcome to join!

Events are held throughout the year to connect students, faculty, and industry in an attempt to further the career goals of declared chemical engineers.

description: Islam's fundamental values of excellence, service, and intellectual curiosity have motivated thousands of American Muslims to pursue careers as physician. description: Since its beginning perhaps more than 15,000 years ago, the discipline of archery has fed mankind, dramatically changed world politics, and has been practiced by a countless number of people. Nearly every culture in the world developed bows, and used them for hunting, combat, and competition. Archery teaches form, precision, relaxation, and strength. name: Asian American Alliance
description: The Asian American Alliance strives to better reflect the Asian-American undergraduate experience and to promote unity and cultural awareness in our community. We hope to promote awareness of Asian American social issues and also to promote our diverse culture by organizing educational and recreational events throughout the academic year.

name: Asian Faculty Association
description: The mission of AFA is to provide a formal networking platform for Asian faculty to foster their growth –personal and professional. The AFA will also serve as the voice to represent and advocate for its members; and to increase the awareness of issues specific to the Asian faculty community.

name: Asian Law Students' Association
description: To foster greater community among Asian law students, create opportunities for mentorship and growth, and celebrate the diversity of Asian cultures.

name: Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association
description: APAMSA at Case Western University School of Medicine aims to improve healthcare for Asians and Pacific Islanders (API) especially Asian immigrants and refugees in the Cleveland metropolitan area. Through community events, we work to foster cultural sensitivity and understanding and encourage student leadership and community engagement on API issues.

name: Association for Computing Machinery
description: CWRU ACM is the campus-wide forum for computing. We connect students across fields and experience levels through recurring conversations, hands-on learning, research and career connections, conferences, and the wider ACM community.

As well as develop a community for students to be a part of. We aim to promote the success of students in the field of computer science and provide opportunities for professional development and collaboration.

name: Association of Women for Mathematics
description: The purpose of the Association for Women in Mathematics is to create a community in which women can thrive in their mathematical endeavors, and to promote equitable opportunity and treatment of women and other gender minorities across the mathematical sciences at Case Western Reserve University.

Nearly every part of the car is designed and built on campus, and our members gain valuable engineering skills beyond what is learned in the classroom. We welcome everyone regardless of major, so make sure to stop by! General Body meetings are held Mondays and Wednesdays at 6 PM, and Saturdays at 12 PM in our workspace on the 5th floor of Sears think[box].

We aim to offer accessible hands-on crafting events where members can learn new skills, express themselves, and create pieces for both personal keeping and local charity initiatives. Through these activities, we seek to cultivate a creative and supportive environment for all students, regardless of prior artistic background.

We are an honors organization for accounting students. Each week we have professional speakers from public accounting and industry come in to speak to our members. Our chapter also gives back to the community through volunteer events at the Cleveland Foodbank, Ronald McDonald House, and in the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance IRS program regularly.

These games will permit participants to create new friendships by interacting and forming connections in a fun, non-academic setting. We strive to inspire and uplift underrepresented communities, providing hope and pathways for future generations to pursue careers in nursing.

This community consists of Kusch House, Glaser House, and Michelson House. Being near the Cedar-Fairmount area, residents have access to a local grocery store, bakeries and many restaurants within walking distance.

Through cultural events, feasts, festivals, and storytelling, we aim to foster a sense of belonging among Bengalis on campus, while sharing our rich heritage with the broader university community.

We hope to foster a tight knit community with students who have similar goals through fundraising, guest speaker seminars, and providing research/volunteering opportunities.

We are partnered with the Cuyahoga County Juvenile Detention Center (CCJDC) and have implemented a mentoring program that provides students with opportunities to explore their career interests. Our sessions are intended to supplement the youth's school curriculum with career-focused activities to inspire them to take initiative in their own education. We work with the youths in small groups to encourage our students to build long-lasting and meaningful relationships.

We would also like to provide the campus and Greater Cleveland community with an opportunity to learn more about the cultural significance of this dance. Our goal is to also establish a well-developed team that provides it's members with a positive, healthy, and welcoming environment.

name: Case College Republicans
description: The purpose of the organization will be to promote free speech and the expression of all points of view, engage in constructive debate, discuss politics, and contribute to an informed student body at Case Western Reserve University.

name: Case Comprehensive Cancer Center
description: The Case Comprehensive Cancer Center (Case CCC) based at Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) is a partnership organization supporting cancer-related research efforts at CWRU, University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, and Cleveland Clinic.

name: Case Crew
description: Crew is a club that provides the opportunity to row on the Cuyahoga River each day. Whether you've rowed all of high school or never touched a boat before, crew is dedicated to helping people learn and develop their rowing skills. We compete across the midwest in both the Fall and Spring seasons, attending regattas such as Knecht Cup, Head of the Ohio, and Head of the Schuylkill. name: Case Cubers
description: Just a place for people to chill and learn how to cube or have fun. Currently, most of our communication is through our Discord server. Join here: https://discord.gg/25ZExrrhm9

name: Case Engineers Council
description: The Case Engineers Council is a unique organization on campus that connects the engineering departments, student organizations, and students passionate about engineering. We promote the collaboration of alumni, faculty, and students through community outreach, company networking, discussions, lectures, and social events.

name: Case for Life
description: Case for Life's mission is to build a culture of life. We work to protect and promote respect for all human life from conception to natural death. We seek to educate ourselves and others on issues concerning the dignity of life, especially abortion. Through outreach and peaceful dialogue, we hope to reach a mutual understanding with those who hold opposing views. We strive to build this mutual understanding for the betterment of individuals' engagement with the topic, and for the broader public dialogue surrounding it. We believe it is our duty to strive to end the violence of abortion; howeve

name: Case for Sight
description: Case for Sight is a vision advocacy group aimed at spreading eye care awareness throughout the CWRU and Cleveland community. This is accomplished through service and philanthropy efforts with various organizations such as the Cleveland Sight Center, MedWish MedWorks, Foundation Fighting Blindness, and ORBIS International. Our annual Dinner in the Dark draws students and professionals from Northeast Ohio to advance vision health in the community.

name: Case Glee Club
description: The Case Glee Club is Case Western Reserve University's premier lower voice ensemble. We focus on singing barbershop-style harmony and TTBB choral music, along with classic pop, world, and gospel pieces. Founded in 1897 at the Case Institute of Technology, we are the oldest student-run organization on campus. We have been a staple of singing tradition at Case Western Reserve University for over 125 years.

name: Case In Point
description: Case in Point (CiP), founded in 2001, is Case Western Reserve University's premiere co-ed a cappella group.\ In the tradition of a cappella music, every sound you hear is produced solely by the human voice (and hands). Additionally, every song we perform is arranged by a current or former member of the group.\ While the faces of Case in Point change over the years, we continue to bring you exciting new a cappella arrangements of a wide variety of music.\ CiP performs at numerous events on and off the CWRU campus. To contact us for your event, please use our contact email listed on this page.\

name: Case Iranian Society
description: This cultural organization is focused on sharing the rich Iranian culture with the entire CWRU community. CIS is trying to unite the Iranian students and maintain the rich ethnic and cultural heritage of the Iranian culture. CIS is providing opportunities and a forum for Iranians to be united within the CWRU community. CIS is committed to creating an environment where its members can interact, have fun, and help each other to become one big family. We encourage both Persians and those from other cultures to join us.

name: Case Kismat Fusion Dance Team
description: Case Kismat is a competitive team that performs fusion dance routines on the Case Western Reserve campus and represents the university at national intercollegiate fusion dance competitions. Each competition that Kismat attends supports a distinct charity that helps underserved populations in India (i.e. Women In Need, Shanti Bhavan Children's Project). Fusion dance, which has an established competition culture in colleges across the country, combines various dance styles. These distinct styles of dance come not just from different regions within India but from around the world. Kismat incorpor

name: Case Liquid Propulsions Team
description: The Case Liquid Propulsion Team (CLPT) is an engineering team founded on providing exciting, relevant, and cutting-edge industry experience for students at CWRU. The club aims to provide students with challenging, interdisciplinary engineering opportunities to grow professionally and individually. CLPT aims to positively contribute to the Midwest talent pool and prepare future engineers to tackle problems confidently. Additionally, CLPT aspires to be recognized across the United States as a team pushing the boundaries of engineering by competing in the Lander Challenge in 2027. The short term

name: Case Listens
description: The mission of CaseListens is to create an environment where students can explore diverse viewpoints on political, religious, and general beliefs in a respectful and constructive manner. By facilitating both large and small events, the club aims to reduce campus tensions and foster understanding across ideological divides.

name: Case Med Book Club
description: Our mission is to build community through our love of reading - creating a welcoming space, where everyone can connect, laugh, and learn together. We want to use the power of stories to spark meaningful conversations, friendship, and have a way to destress from the rigors of medical school.

name: Case Med Casual Sports
description: To promote wellness and activity in the form of casual sports in the sun for medical students.

name: Case Med Climbs
description: Our goal is to connect medical students through rock climbing in a fun, inclusive, and welcoming environment. We organize bouldering and top-rope activities at local climbing gyms. No climbing experience is required to participate and we encourage students of all skill levels to join us on our climbing outings.

name: Case Med Community Hoops
description: Case Med Community Hoops is an organization at Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine whose mission is to bring community, mentorship, and fun to youth through basketball.

name: Case Med Community Kitchen
description: Case Med Community Kitchen is a medical student organization that aims to work alongside other established programs to provide meals, supplies, and resources to unhoused communities in the Cleveland area. By gathering together to prepare meals for those in need, we hope to not only provide assistance and nutrition, but to also foster lasting bonds with our local community.

name: Case Med for Health Literacy
description: CaseMed for Health Literacy is a student group committed to benefiting the local Cleveland community by addressing various health concerns related to education. We are also dedicated to engaging medical students in areas of community service related to health education and to helping students communicate health topics more effectively.

name: Case Med Pride
description: Our mission is to promote awareness and understanding of the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) and all sexual and gender minority (SGM) communities through our committees spanning across advocacy, mentorship and professional development, education, and social and wellness.

name: Case Med Special Olympics
description: We partner with Special Olympics Ohio and community allies to deliver barrier‑free, athlete‑centered programming that blends foundational sport skills, adaptive coaching, and culturally sensitive health care. Central to our work are hands‑on, supervised clinics where athletes practice skills in real time and CWRU members learn applied, neurodiversity affirming coaching. There will also be opportunities to provide physicals and health care, and family‑centered communication.

name: Case Med Tabletop Society
description: Case Med Tabletop Society is a student initiative that brings together members of the Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine community through board games. We host game nights and events that provide students with an opportunity to meet new people and enjoy some friendly competition outside of the classroom. Whether you are new to board games or an experienced player, everyone is welcome to join and play!

name: Case Motorcycle Club
description: Case Motorcycle Club has been created to offer a space for students to come together to learn about, discuss and practice safe motorcycle admiring, riding habits and techniques as well as motorcycle maintenance practices.

name: Case Nepali Student Organization
description: 1.2.1 To promote interactions among students and friends of Nepal by organizing social and cultural events. 1.2.2 To help Nepali students adjust to a new cultural and academic environment. 1.2.3 To highlight social and economic issues facing disadvantaged groups and reach through informed and impactful community service efforts. 1.2.4 To engage in fundraising activities to financially support disadvantaged groups in Nepal 1.2.5 To establish and promote mentorship and networking efforts within Case Western Reserve University and Nepali communities.

name: Case Neuroscience Society
description: Case Neuroscience Society is sponsored by the Department of Neuroscience of the Case Medical School. This club began intending to create a niche in which interested students can learn & teach each other, gain exposure to lab techniques, and attend networking events, talks, and seminars. We hope you see this club as a light practice for the skills you will need in developing aspects of your career, whether in medicine, science, law, or engineering.

name: Case Quantum Computing
description: The CQC club aims to provide resources and a community for anyone interested in quantum computing and quantum information science. Through workshops, hackathons, and connections with professionals, we will provide opportunities to learn about and get involved with this rapidly growing field.

name: Case Reserve Review
description: To represent and uplift the creative voices of students at CWRU and in the greater Cleveland community

name: Case Rocket Team
description: Case Rocket Team [CRT] enables students interested in aerospace and rocketry to construct their own rockets and compete in international collegiate high power rocketry competitions. We are one of the university's engineering design teams, located on Think[box] 5th Floor. No experience is necessary to join, and we welcome members from all majors.

name: Case School of Engineering
description: Case School of Engineering is one of eight academic hubs at Case Western Reserve University—one of the nation’s leading research universities. Here, the academic and research experiences are as robust as our longstanding history. Our location in Cleveland, Ohio—a center of cultural, business and healthcare activity—offers unparalleled access to engaging academic, research, clinical, entrepreneurial and volunteer opportunities.

name: Case Sound Society
description: Open to all genres and skill levels, Case Sound Society is CWRU's community for music producers.

name: Case Sports Analytics Association
description: The purpose of the Case Sports Analytics Association (CSAA) is to promote interest in sports analytics, teach members the basics of sports analytics, work on analytical projects, and join analytics competitions.

name: Case STEM Educate
description: The Case STEM Educate (CSE) aims to pique scientific interest in the underprivileged youth by creating engaging, interactive and easy-to-understand academic resources. Several systematic barriers, such as fewer compelling academic resources, family background, and lack of mentorship opportunities, prevent students from developing an inclination towards STEM. CSE aims to mitigate this disparity by creating accessible and interesting online resources such as interactive textbooks containing interesting illustrations and videos; ultimately making the idea of "science" truly appealing for younger

name: Case Surgical Society
description: The Case Surgical Society (CSS) serve as a means for students interested in the surgical field of medicine to learn more about surgery. CSS is a strong advocate for experiential learning, and we will provide hands-on learning experiences with using suturing instruments and practice suturing on suture mats. CSS will also teach students about different suturing and surgical techniques, surgical specialties, and what it means to pursue a career in surgery. Join CSS to gain valuable suturing experience and knowledge about surgery to prepare for your future endeavors in health care.

name: Case Trading Card Game Club
description: Trading Card Game (TCG) is a popular hobby that allows players to collect unique playing cards, build their own creative deck, and compete with other players in an exciting turn-based match against their opponent's decks. Some of the most popular TCGs include Magic The Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game, and Pokemon Trading Card Game, with an ever-growing popularity of virtual TCGs such as Heartstone as well. Much like a sport, the competitive nature of this hobby requires a community of players who can play with one another, cooperate in critical thinking to discover the best deck recipes

name: CaseMed Golf Association
description: The mission of the CaseMed Golf Association is to provide an organized avenue for medical students and faculty members to connect with each other and to the Cleveland community through the game of golf.

name: CaseMed Harm Reduction
description: Case Med for Harm Reduction is dedicated to promoting health, safety, and well-being within the Cleveland community by providing comprehensive harm reduction education. Through collaboration with local organizations, healthcare professionals, and community leaders, we work to reduce the negative effects of substance use and other high-risk behaviors. Our mission is to empower individuals with the knowledge, tools, and resources they need to make informed decisions, while fostering a compassionate and non-judgmental environment that supports prevention, education, and access to critical service

name: CaseMed Minute
description: Our mission is to enhance the quality of Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine students’ education by providing concise educational videos on high-yield concepts introduced throughout the WR2 curriculum. We aim to establish an efficient space of learning amidst the high volume of medical knowledge and refine these resources for future students.

description: The Center for Career Success is here to help students, alumni and employers. Through events, coaching, assessments, and other resources, our staff can help you define and reach your goals. Please visit our website at: https://case.edu/studentlife/careercenter/ For events related to your career search, postgraduate education planning, networking with employers and more, log in to Handshake at cwru.joinhandshake.com.

name: Center for Civic Engagement & Learning

name: Center For Global Health and Infectious Diseases
description: The Center for Global Health & Infectious Diseases (GHID) aims to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, research, and innovation in addressing global infectious diseases. We bring together researchers, healthcare professionals, and students to share knowledge, promote cutting-edge discoveries, and develop solutions to global health challenges

description: The Center’s activities have four objectives: (1) to make Case Western Reserve University a continually more attractive and rewarding institution for students and faculty who wish to learn about and engage in the creation of public policy; (2) to raise the public profile of the University by sponsoring programs and other activities that publicize and increase the reach of the work of CWRU’s policy analysts and their guests; (3) to contribute to the wider community by disseminating information and analysis of policy issues as generated both by CWRU faculty and by guests whom we bring to campus;

name: Center on Trauma and Adversity
description: The mission of the Center on Trauma and Adversity is to reduce the impact of trauma, respond to adversity, and promote resilience through trauma-informed integrated research and training.

We aim to create a relaxed and inspiring atmosphere for members to build their clay sculpting and design skills. Students will have the opportunity to design ceramic products of their own choice, such as mugs, planters, and various types of decorations. This organization will occasionally hold trips to the nearby art museums.

We work to bring the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering together as a community through regular discussions and social events.

Meetings are every Thursday 7-9 PM in the Senior Classroom of the Tinkham Veale University Center (11038 Bellflower Rd., Cleveland, OH).

description: Cleveland Safety-Net Collective is a medical student-led organization focused on strengthening Cleveland’s safety-net healthcare system through a close partnership with the Salaam Clinic, a free clinic serving uninsured communities, predominantly refugees and immigrants. name: Cooking Club
description: Students of all cultural backgrounds and identifications can be united together through the joy of cooking. Register beforehand on Campusgroups, and if you can no longer attend, be sure to cancel! - No equipment necessary (except for Tupperware if you'd like to bring back your leftovers)

name: Corporate Finance & Law Alliance
description: The Corporate Finance & Law Alliance (CFLA) is an organization based out of the CWRU School of Law. The group serves two primary purposes. First, it organizes networking events for law students, business students, and other members of the CWRU community to connect with local business professionals. Second, it educates it members by hosting lunchtime informational speeches at the law school, typically on financial literacy or some financial/corporate law topic.

name: Cracking the Case Mystery Book Club
description: This is not your ordinary book club: our specialty is the mystery genre. We will read a variety of mystery novels from traditional whodunits to suspenseful thrillers, watch mystery-themed TV shows and movies, and convene with our fellow detectives on a regular basis for discussions. At the end of the semester, we host a murder mystery dinner party so that you can test your sleuthing abilities in real time (and enjoy delicious food!). Together, we will hone our investigative skills while inspiring the next generation of young detectives.

name: CraftCare Studio

In everything we do, we challenge them to think beyond the possible.

name: Cricket Club
description: Cricket is a bat and ball game that originated in England around 1300. It is now played in more than 100 countries around the world. It requires team play which helps people boost team spirit. CWRU cricket club strives to provide safe, secure and friendly environment in which students can learn and play the game of cricket and develop their skills, to promote fair play, respect for all and observance of the laws and the spirit of cricket

description: The goal of the CCIG is to connect interested medical students with critical care professionals and to give them opportunities to practice skills that may be helpful for a career in critical care.

We aim to not focus solely on specific topics such as the affordability of healthcare, but to recognize all of its facets. By facilitating mentorship and networking, we connect students with experienced professionals, creating a supportive community.

We believe that students can impact our campus community in profound ways and we strive to provide the learning opportunities, support and institutional knowledge to make that happen!

description: Case Western Reserve University Department of Human Resources acknowledges that people are our most valuable asset for sustaining excellent teaching, research, service, and attracting a talented workforce. We hope to work with young students in schools and other organizations surrounding the CWRU campus. Our mission is to provide opportunities to learn directly from practicing endocrinologists, connect students with research and shadowing experiences, and promote volunteer involvement in the local community. Co-op also gives you a head start on your job search since many companies hire their co-op students in full-time positions after graduation.

name: Equestrian Club

The engagement will be open to any one of any experience level and open for anyone to join at any time.

We also work closely with other food and service related groups to connect multiple student organizations together through Food Forum.

We hope to help bridge the gap in global healthcare by delivering dental services, education, and resources to countries with limited access to dental care. In creating an atmosphere of teamwork among students, professionals, and local communities, we seek to improve oral healthcare and create sustainable impact.

We seek to provide early exposure to a variety of surgical fields and help students build connections in the surgical community. We regularly hold lectures, workshops, panels, and other events in order to expose students to different elements of a career in surgery. In addition, we connect students with mentors at different time points in their careers through structured mentorship and shadowing opportunities.

Sessions address topics such as safety, building a support network, belonging, love, forgiveness, self-esteem, knowledge and education, and self-actualization.

description: The Minority Business Alliance offers networking, professional development, career advancement, and community service opportunities in a welcoming environment for current and potential minority students of the Weatherhead School of Management at Case Western Reserve University. We strive to fulfill the unique personal and professional needs that enable minorities to maximize their career potential in business.

name: Minority Association for Premedical Students
description: MAPS is one of Case's most diverse, pre-medical, student-run organization on campus that aims to help pre-medical students on their journey to medical school in a variety of ways. MAPS is the Case Western Reserve University chapter of the Minority Association of Pre-medical Students (MAPS). MAPS works closely with its sister organization SNMA, which is a group of CWRU medical school students who act as inspiration, mentors, and friends to any members of the MAPS group.

description: Programming, advocacy, and leadership development in the Mistletoe Community

name: Mistletoe Residential Community
description: To create a living and learning community suitable for holistic growth and self-development.

name: Model United Nations
description: Model United Nations is a competitive intercollegiate foreign and public affairs activity that seeks to develop delegates' skills with public speaking, diplomatic compromise, resolution writing, group leadership, and the accurate representation of a nation's foreign policies while fostering a greater understanding of how the United Nations works, the cultural, political, and economic backgrounds of other nations, and the foreign affairs community in general.

name: Model United Nations Home Team
description: This page is for internal use only. Please refer to the main Model United Nations page for information on the club.

name: Molecular Biology and Microbiology Graduate Student Council
description: The purpose of the Council is to serve as the representative body for graduate students in the Case Western Reserve University Department of Molecular Biology and Microbiology. It aims to promote the interests, welfare, and academic development of graduate students within the department by facilitating effective communication, fostering a sense of community, and advocating for their needs and concerns.

name: Moll Institute for Mental Health and Well-Being
description: The Sara and Curt Moll Institute for Mental Health and Well-Being is dedicated to addressing the growing need for excellent mental health care in Northeast Ohio and beyond. The institute aims to collaborate across disciplines and perspectives at Case Western Reserve University and in our community to improve the effectiveness of mental health care and increase access to services and providers.

name: Mortar Board Honor Society Lux Chapter
description: As a part of the national Mortar Board Honor Society, the Lux Chapter aims to provide opportunities for leadership, service, and scholarship through recognition of student achievements in those departments.

name: MTG at CWRU
description: The Medical Technology Group at Case Western Reserve University promotes design and education through collaborations between undergraduate students and practicing clinicians in the pursuit of a comprehensive approach to medical technology development that meets a relevant clinical need. We aim to generate solutions to these medical problems, not only developing prototypes to meet the needs of patients and clinicians, but assessing the ultimate market viability of our proposed solutions.

name: Murray Hill Community
description: Murray Hill is informally known as "Bottom of the Hill," due to it's placement at the base of the Carlton Road community. Being near Cleveland's "Little Italy" neighborhood, residents are in walking distance of many restaurants and bakeries. The complex is located in the South Residential Village and consists of Alumni House, Howe House, Staley House, and Tippit House.

name: Murray Hill Community Council
description: Programming, advocacy, and leadership development in the Murray Hill Community

name: Music Graduate Student Association
description: The Music Graduate Student Association works to provide sustained support for current and prospective graduate students in the Department of Music at Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) in all aspects of graduate life. We foster intellectual and professional development through sponsorship of academic events and discussion, and promote fellowship among the graduate students through social events and moral support. We also encourage prospective students to join the program by coordinating campus visits and compiling informative materials about the program. One of our principal goals is that

name: Music Undergraduate Student Involvement Committee
description: The Music Undergraduate Student Involvement Committee (M.U.S.I.C.) club at CWRU promotes and facilitates musical collaborations, performances, and camaraderie across campus among music majors, non-majors, faculty, and the general public.

name: Muslim Law Students Association
description: Our mission is to advocate for Muslim students in the law school community.

name: Muslim Student Association
description: The Muslim Student Association (MSA) at Case aims to provide a home away from home for Muslim students on campus by organizing various religious and cultural events throughout the year. These events are open to all Case students, staff and faculty as well as family members regardless of their religious, cultural and ethnic background. Our organization reaches out to everyone who is interested in learning about Islam and embraces the concepts of harmony in diversity, peace and fellowship,. Besides religious and cultural events, MSA activities also include social and community service projects.

name: Naach Di CWRU
description: Naach Di CWRU promotes South Asian culture through performance and outreach, expanding the reach of our culture through Northeast Ohio. As a nationally renowned dance competition, we aim to create an experience that our participants and audience alike can enjoy and experience. The collegiate dance circuit is full of competitions across the United States, but our motto is ÔÇ£For dancers, by dancersÔÇØ and we cater directly to our dancers. description: The mission for Naadam is to create an established space where students who learn and appreciate Indian Classical Music can express their cultural heritage. We want to spread awareness of Indian culture and foster an understanding of Indian Classical Music among the Case Western Reserve University community.

name: National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) on Campus
description: NAMI, the National Alliance on Mental Illness, is the nation's largest grassroots mental health organization dedicated to building better lives for the millions of Americans affected by mental illness. NAMI advocates for access to services, treatment, supports and research and is steadfast in its commitment to raising awareness and building a community of hope for all those in need. name: National Arab American Medical Association NextGen
description: NAAMA NextGen aims to bring together MENA medical students and help them with their career goals in the context of their MENA identity.

name: National Lawyer's Guild
description: The National Lawyers Guild is the oldest nationwide progressive bar association that primarily advocates for prison abolition and protestor rights. NLG is well-known for its legal observer program, in which laypeople can get trained to record police misconduct at protests.

name: National Society of Black Engineers
description: NSBE's mission statement is to increase the number of culturally responsible Black Engineers who exceed academically, succeed professionally, and positively impact the community. We have meetings every 2 weeks where we share valuable information for developing young professionals. NSBE puts on professional and engaging events. Our professional events connect students with professionals in the area for mentoring and the opportunity to gain corporate experience. The highlight of the year for our members is always the national conference where there is a large career fair and multiple workshops.

name: National Student Speech Language Hearing Association
description: We are a pre-professional club for students interested in the Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) major and those interested in fields such as speech language pathology, audiology, psychology, education, medical fields etc. We hold informative events led by professionals within the field of CSD, raise awareness for communication disorders, volunteer in the Cleveland community, and attend networking conferences. All are welcome to join!

name: National Youth Sports Program
description: The National Youth Sports Program at Case Western Reserve is an annual five-week summer comprehensive experience that combines fitness, fun, and learning. During NYSP local community youth NYSP staff utilize sports participation and academic programs to promote self-respect and healthy living skills necessary for participants' life-long success.

name: Needle-Felting Club
description: Our group's mission is to give students the resources, instruction, and encouraging environment to create their own projects of items they are unable to buy. Our club wishes for our members to have the guidance and peer-support to create their own creative projects that they are passionate about without having to purchase them online, travel far-away to buy them in-person, use copious amounts of plastic filament to 3d print the few models they can find online, and be unable to customize these trinkets in anyway. Needle-felting addresses all of these issues and students may grow their own confi

name: Network for Environmental and Medical Outreach
description: The mission of NEMO is to provide students at Case Western Reserve University the opportunity to teach the case community and the surrounding Cleveland area the importance of environmental health, fundraise for worthy causes, and speak out against public policy deleterious to environmental health and public health.

name: Neuroscience Graduate Student Organization
description: The mission of the NGSO is to promote and educate graduate students about the field of neuroscience. We strive to provide graduate students of all backgrounds with educational, mentorship and networking opportunities that serve to bolster their professional aspirations. Additionally, we will provide resources that establish and promote a cohesive, inclusive and productive community for members.

name: Neurotechnology Club
description: We want students who are interested in neurotechnology (specifically brain computer interfaces) to be able to work on relevant projects in a team setting, and have access to a community of people who share the same interest. The club values hands-on learning and seeks to address real world problems with innovative solutions.

name: Newman Catholic Student Association
description: Newman Catholic Student Association (NCSA) is a Catholic faith community open to all Case Western students. Come join us as we explore how to integrate our faith with our studies and life. We combine the riches of millennia of Catholic Tradition with a warm, fun and friendly community where all are truly welcome. Whether you were born and raised Catholic, or would just like to learn more about Catholicism; or whether you are embarking on your first year at Case, your last, or even post-graduate studies; we invite you to come to any of our events and learn more about NCSA, Catholicism, faith an

name: NextGen Network
description: The <40 Network unites, connects and empowers CWRU’s faculty & staff across disciplines, departments, and areas of campus. This network is a resource for early and mid-career faculty and staff looking to build relationships, exchange perspectives, and foster a sense of community. By providing support for young professionals in navigating the journey of working in higher education and bringing diverse voices together, we aim to support one another and grow together as a university community.

name: Nigerian Student Association
description: NSA will act as a welcoming environment for those that are Nigerian or those who wish to learn more about Nigerian culture.

name: Novel Notions
description: Case Western Reserve University and members of CWRU Novel Notions seek to create a comforting environment for all kinds of literature lovers through informative and thought-provoking dialogue surrounding a common reading for the month. This club aims to bring those with similar passions for reading into cohesive and thoughtful discussions while sharing that same passion for literature through community outreach and increasing the accessibility of books in underserved areas of Cleveland. description: The purpose of Nu Rho Psi shall be to: (1) encourage professional interest and excellence in scholarship, particularly in neuroscience; (2) award recognition to students who have achieved such excellence in scholarship; (3) advance the discipline of neuroscience; (4) encourage intellectual and social interaction between students, faculty, and professionals in neuroscience and related fields; (5) promote career development in neuroscience and related fields; (6) increase public awareness of neuroscience and its benefits for the individual and society; and (7) encourage service to the community.

name: Obstetrics and Gynecology Interest Group
description: Our mission is to provide opportunities for medical students to learn about topics related to the field of Obstetrics and Gynecology, connect with faculty members and engage in outreach efforts within the greater Cleveland community.

description: The Office of Accommodated Testing & Services (OATS) provides accommodations as determined by Disability Resources for undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. The services offered through OATS include testing accommodations, note-taking services, and assistive technology.

name: Office of Energy & Sustainability
description: CWRU's Office for Sustainability helps with sustainability initiatives on campus, we champion the climate action plan, energy efficiency, recycling, composting in our cafeterias and many other initiatives to reduce the University's environmental footprint. We hope to create a positive change to the world through our operations, and daily interactions, and are constantly thinking about ways to improve the state of sustainability at the university. The office partners and collaborates with many other departments on campus, with off-campus organizations, and with student organizations to sponsor

name: Office of Equity
description: The mission of Office for Equity at Case Western Reserve University is to facilitate the academic and personal success of students and employees who have survived, experienced or are experiencing sexual harassment, as well as sexual violence and other kinds of discrimination and harassment. Equity does this by reaching out to students who have had these experiences and offering support, including connections to mental health or advocacy or other resources, and academic support. name: Office of Events and Programs
description: Innovative programming and engaging lectures generate the cultural vibrancy that is at the core the University Circle experience. From enlightened beginnings each academic year at Fall Convocation to celebrations of great minds at Commencement, the Office of Events and Programs manages the large, public ceremonies and events that have campus-wide significance.

name: Office of General Counsel
description: OGC helps to advance the mission of CWRU by providing legal services to the institution.

description: In accordance with the Case Western Reserve University Strategic Plan, Think Big, The Office of Government and Community Relations is committed to strengthening its relationships with public officials and community stakeholders, increasing the visibility of the university throughout Ohio and nationally and increasing the resources for university initiatives. name: Office of Graduate Student Life
description: The mission of the Office of Graduate Student Life is to provide a vibrant graduate student experience through access to information and services available at CWRU and create opportunities to build community, foster conversations, and encourage collaboration across disciplines.

name: Office of Institutional Research
description: To provide accurate, consistent, and timely information about Case Western Reserve and its external environment to constituents within and outside the university. We also develop and carry out a comprehensive program of research and analysis to support strategic planning, assessment, evaluation, and institutional decision-making.

name: Office of Interprofessional Education
description: To truly address the complex health and well-being challenges of our communities, we must cultivate a Case Culture of Interprofessional Excellence. By investing in CWRU health science culture, we prepare and empower our integrated healthcare students to bridge disciplines and solve the challenges facing our communities.

name: Office of Multicultural Affairs
description: OUR PLEDGE Is to enhance the harmony of the diverse, multi-ethnic CWRU community through maximizing the mutual acceptance of all individuals. OUR MISSION To encourage, support and facilitate the success of all CWRU students by providing opportunities for diverse interaction and cultural education that occurs outside the classroom environment.

name: Office of Research and Technology Management
description: The Office of Research and Technology Management provides support to seek out grant funding, manage research projects responsibly, and to transfer university technologies to the marketplace. Case Western Reserve is a place for people driven to make a difference, and our office exists to help them succeed.

name: Office of Student Activities & Leadership
description: The Office of Student Activities and Leadership is CWRU's campus resource for student organizational needs and leadership opportunities. Located in the Tinkham Veale University Center, SA&L serves both undergraduate and graduate students through resources ranging from programming & event planning to highly involved opportunities such as the Emerging Leaders Program. Events throughout the year include Hudson Relays, Homecoming, Relay for Life, and Strengthsmonth. Stop by our office to learn more! Office: Tinkham Veale University Center 148 Phone: (216) 368-2679

name: Office of the Provost
description: Providing leadership that supports all aspects of the academic enterprise of Case Western Reserve and assuring that resources are aligned with the academic goals of the university.

name: Office of the University Registrar
description: The Office of the Registrar at Case Western Reserve University is committed to ensuring the integrity, security, and longevity of academic records; providing support and leadership for the Student Information System (SIS); and leading and supporting the implementation of academic policy. Our office provides official transcripts, degree and enrollment verifications, support for students utilizing Veterans Benefits, and SIS resource support to students, staff, and faculty.

name: Ohio Cardiovascular and Diabetes Health Collaborative
description: Founded in 2017, Cardi-OH is a statewide collaborative of health care professionals who share best practices to improve cardiovascular and diabetes outcomes and eliminate disparities.

name: Ohio Collegiate Music Education Association
description: OCMEA is a group comprised primarily of music education majors. OCMEA offers professional development and networking opportunities for those involved and interested in the field of music education. OCMEA also coordinates transportation and fundraising for the OMEA music education conference every spring semester, providing undergraduates with learning and networking opportunities. OCMEA's mission is to provide students with professional development opportunities in the field of music education, while also creating a welcoming and close-knit group of members.

name: Ohio Student Association
description: We organize young people to build independent political power and work together in an intergenerational movement for racial, social, economic and educational justice. This involves educating people on current issues in the communities they live in and empowering them through voting, canvassing, petitioning, and more.

name: Older Wiser Law Students
description: To help facilitate non traditional law students form a community of support and a place for talking through issues associated with their status.

name: Oncology Interest Group
description: To foster a community of medical students with interests in the field of oncology.

name: Operations & Supply Chain Club

name: Ophthalmology Interest Group
description: The Ophthalmology Interest Group exists to explore medical student interests in the specialty of Ophthalmology. This includes activities such as setting up shadowing, research, and clinical experiences as well as organizing Q&A sessions with matched M4s and ophthalmologists.

name: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Club
description: To create an environment where students can learn about Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, and improve their surgical skills.

name: Order of Omega
description: Order of Omega is a national honorary society recognizing outstanding leadership in the Greek community. Order of Omega at Case Western Reserve University is in charge of allocating the Emergency Dues Fund to those Greek community members who need the support and facilitating the Academy, a leadership retreat for rising leaders in the Greek community.

name: Orientation and New Student Transitions
description: The Office of Orientation and New Student Transitions supports the successful academic and social transition of new students to the Case Western Reserve University community.

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship
description: This student group is a student chapter (hereafter Chapter) recognized by Orthodox Christian Fellowship, a California nonprofit corporation with its principal offices in Brookline, Massachusetts and which is an agency of the Assembly of Canonical Orthodox Bishops in the United States. The purpose of the Chapter, as articulated in the Charter, is to offer college students rich community in Christ, inspiring life-long love of God and neighbor. This is accomplished through cultivating a campus community of worship, witness, service, fellowship, and education.

name: Orthopedic Interest Group
description: The Orthopaedic Surgery Interest Group (OIG) aims to cultivate student interest in the field of orthopaedic surgery through educational events, mentorship opportunities, and research involvement. Our mission is to provide a platform for medical students to explore musculoskeletal medicine, develop technical and clinical skills, and connect with faculty, residents, and peers dedicated to advancing patient care through innovation and compassion.

name: oSTEM
description: oSTEM @ CWRU empowers LGBTQ+ people in STEM to succeed personally, academically, and professionally by cultivating environments and communities that nurture innovation, leadership, and advocacy.

name: Pakistan Graduate Student Association
description: The Pakistan Graduate Student Association (PGSA) exists to build a supportive community for Pakistani graduate students on campus, helping members navigate academic, professional, and personal life abroad while celebrating Pakistani culture and heritage. Through social events, mentorship, and academic support, PGSA aims to foster friendship among its members, promote cultural understanding within the wider university community, and serve as a resource network for new and prospective Pakistani students transitioning to graduate study in the CWRU.

name: Pakistani Student Association
description: The Pakistani Student Association (PSA) at Case Western Reserve University is dedicated to promoting cultural understanding and fostering a strong sense of community among Pakistani students. We strive to provide a platform for cultural exchange, host educational events, and champion diversity and inclusiveness within the campus community. Through our efforts, we aim to create a welcoming environment that celebrates Pakistani heritage and contributes to a vibrant, multicultural campus.

name: Palestine Children's Relief Fund: Case Western Reserve University Chapter
description: Palestine Children’s Relief Fund (PCRF) is a worldwide established nonprofit organization regularly sending injured and sick Middle Eastern children to North and South America, other parts of the Middle East, and Europe for free and specialized healthcare not available to them. We locate, sponsor, and run international volunteer medical missions to the Middle East. PCRF at CWRU serves to expand the virtue of this foundation and guide the people who are willing to volunteer a helping hand or helping dollar.

name: Palliative Medicine Interest Group
description: As the Palliative Medicine Interest Group, we strive to provide education to our medical school community about palliative medicine and end of life care. We seek to do this by connecting students with educational materials and clinical opportunities in the field to learn about the provider experience.

name: Paper Airplanes
description: The purpose of this organization is to connect students of the Case Western Reserve University community with individuals affected by conflict and displacement through free, one-on-one virtual language and skills tutoring. Our chapter supports Paper Airplanes’ mission to promote cross-cultural understanding, educational access, and mutual empowerment through one-on-one online lessons, while fostering global citizenship and leadership among our members.

name: Partners In Health Engage
description: The mission of Partners In Health Engage is to fundraise, advocate, and build community for the cause of providing quality healthcare infrastructure in the poorest communities around the world, as well as in our own local communities. We fundraise directly towards our cause, raising money for building clinics, building roads, training healthcare workers from local communities, and maintaining a constant supply of resources to the health systems that we build. name: Paws for a Cause
description: Paws for a Cause “PAC” is a student-led organization aimed at making a positive impact on animals through advocacy for proper care and community involvement. PAC also places focus on student wellness through therapeutic animal interaction, highlighting the importance in human-animal connection. By connecting the Case Western Reserve University “CWRU” community with therapy dogs/cats as well as through volunteering opportunities at local animal shelters and organizations, we encourage the message that all animals deserve to be treated humanely with love, dignity, and respect.

name: Pediatric Dentistry Club
description: Advancing the oral health and overall well-being of children through education, advocacy, and community service.

name: Pediatrics Interest Group
description: The Pediatrics Interest Group educates medical students about the path to residency and career in pediatrics. We act as a liaison to connect medical students with research projects, career counseling, and shadowing as well as volunteer events in the community.

name: Pep Band
description: We are the official Case Western Reserve University Pep Band, a student group devoted to playing music and spreading spirit at events around campus, including basketball and hockey games and other community events. Anyone is welcome - just bring your instrument, come join the fun, and help support our Spartans! If you've got some time, feel free to stop by any of our rehearsals. name: PERIOD @ CWRU
description: PERIOD @ CWRU's mission is to advocate for menstrual care on CWRU's campus and in the Cleveland community. Our goals are to normalize menstruation for all students regardless of gender identity, provide care packages for those in need, and affect legislation by empowering students to raise awareness about the issue and create change.

name: Personal Finance Club
description: To empower CWRU students with the knowledge and skills to make informed financial decisions by promoting financial literacy, fostering discussions about money, and providing practical tools for building long-term financial wellness

description: The GSO fosters the development of graduate students in the Department of Pharmacology.

name: PhD Student Nurses Association

The PSNA's goals include: Supporting scholarly productivity, Socializing students into research roles, Representing PhD students to the PhD Council, and Improving communication.

name: Phi Alpha Delta
description: Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity, International is a professional law fraternity advancing integrity, compassion and courage through service to the student, the school, the profession and the community. Bound together by tradition and our common interest in the law, we share these core values: Integrity, Compassion, Courage, Professionalism, Service, Diversity, and Innovation. PAD has an open membership policy and encourages all interested pre-law students to join!

name: Phi Delta Epsilon
description: Phi Delta Epsilon is an International Medical Fraternity that creates physicians with the guiding principles of philanthropy, deity, and education, through fellowship, service, mentoring, and formal training in leadership, science, and ethics. Our motto is 'Facta Non Verba, Deeds Not Words'; Phi Delta Epsilon welcomes students who are interested in medicine.

name: Phi Delta Theta

Others intend to pursue careers in journalism, nonprofit groups, public policy, government, or business.

name: Pre Dental Society
description: The Pre-Dental Society (PDS) of CWRU is focused on helping pre-dental students reach their goal of becoming a dentist. As a student-run organization, we bring in speakers from the Case School of Dental Medicine, conduct information sessions about recommended paths of dentistry, volunteer in the Cleveland area, and provide valuable resources for our members to improve their dental school applications. description: CWRU PCP is a Primary Care Progress Student Action Network chapter of the Intend Health Strategies national organization that aims to develop an inter-professional network that advocates for primary care progress while practicing civic engagement in order to achieve sustainable community change. Efforts have also focused on donations and fundraising.

The organization is committed to fostering scholarly interest in the specialty, supporting the development of simulated and clinical competence through educational initiatives, training opportunities, and professional growth opportunities to enhance student doctor proficiency and contribute to the improvement of patient care and to the field of prosthodontics. Our goal is to create a supportive infrastructure that enables academic success, professional development, and a thriving educational community.

description: We are a competitive Indian folk dance team which competes at international competitions around the U.S., as well as weddings and events on campus and across Ohio. More importantly, we are a family of students which loves to dance and have fun!

name: Spartan Bicycle Shop
description: The Spartan Bicycle Shop is a non-profit organization located in the Sears ThinkBox (5th floor). We perform basic bicycle repairs, maintenance and provide accessories for purchase. The executive body and its employees run on a voluntary basis - functioning on-demand weekday services to accomodate student scheduling. Operational Profits accrued are to be reinvested in the East Cleveland & Campus Communities via bicycle, monetary donations as well as for cycling infrastructure advocacy.

name: Spartan Cheer
description: Spartan cheerleading is a club sport which aims to promote school spirit and spartan pride at home games for various CWRU varsity teams.

name: Spartan Dance Team
description: Welcome to the Spartan Dance Team's page! We are a team of dancers that promote school spirit. We perform at CWRU football and basketball games, as well as various campus events. If you're interested in joining, feel free to leave us a message or follow us on Instagram @spartandancecwru!

name: Spartan Rugby
description: To represent Case Western Reserve University at the local and national levels as a competitive Rugby team, and to create a strong sense of brotherhood in all our members. We strive to share our passion and love for the sport with all members of the student body.

name: Spartan Running Club
description: The Spartan Running Club is a friendly group of runners in the Case Western community. SRC meets at Freiberger Field four to five times a week for team runs. We hope to foster a love of running in the Case community by welcoming those new to running, interested in getting in shape, or looking to compete in races. For those who want to participate in our road races each semester, we pay in-part the cost of race entry.

name: Spartan Sports Analytics Club
description: The mission of the Spartans Sports Analytics Club is to equip members with practical, real-world data analytics and presentation skills through hands-on work with sports data and technology tools such as Google Colab and Excel. The Club provides members the opportunity to translate data into meaningful insights by presenting analytical findings directly to coaches and athletic staff within their respective organizations. Through this applied, collaborative approach, members develop as well-rounded technologists, communicators, and problem-solvers prepared for careers in analytics, technology,

name: Spartan Tappers
description: The Spartan Tappers are the loudest dance group on campus! We provide two free tap classes every week: a Beginner Class and an Intermediate/Advanced Class. Tapping is a lot of fun and a great workout. Dancers of all levels are welcome! We host Tap on the Lawn every semester and perform at various events around campus!

name: Spartans for the Ronald McDonald House Cleveland
description: Our group's purpose is to facilitate and encourage soda tab collection and donation to the Ronald McDonald House of Cleveland by CWRU undergraduate and graduate students.

name: SpartanTHON
description: SpartanTHON is a year-round fundraising and service organization dedicated to celebrating and saving the lives of the kids at University Hospitals Rainbow Babies and Children's Hospital. SpartanTHON is a non-profit under Children's Miracle Network, specifically Dance Marathon. Our organization develops leaders, engages local businesses, mentors high schools, and plans some of the most successful, impactful, and fun events at CWRU. SpartanTHON puts volunteering with Rainbow and many campus engagement events throughout the year to raise awareness and funds for children and families impacted by c

name: Special Care Dentistry Association
description: The American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry defines special healthcare needs as "any physical, development, mental, sensory, behavioral, cognitive or emotional impairment or limiting condition that requires medical management, healthcare intervention, and/or use of specialized services or programs." The Special Care Dentistry Club seeks to provide dental students of Case Western Reserve University valuable experiences of working with people with special needs by offering increased awareness, attention, adaptation and education on accommodating measures beyond routine treatment. Moreover, this

name: Spikeball Club
description: Spikeball can best be described as a mix between four square and volleyball. The club is open to anyone who wants to try something new and entertaining, those with prior experience, or even those simply looking for a fun way to work out.

name: Spoken English Programs and SELP Tutoring
description: The Spoken English Programs and SELP Tutoring offer FREE spoken English tutoring and events across campus to help members of the campus community enhance spoken English skills and understanding of culture

name: Sports & Entertainment Law Society
description: The purpose of the Sports & Entertainment Law Society (SELS), is to provide members, alumni, and all organizational stakeholders with insight and education on key legal issues encountered in the sports, film, television, and music entertainment business segments, while also providing members with unique opportunities to connect, engage, and cultivate industry relationships. The Sports & Entertainment Law Society will deliver on these objectives in two important ways. First, SELS will provide participants with information, resources, and access to successful industry professionals who will shar

name: Sports Medicine Club
description: To promote interest, education, and professional development in the fields of sports medicine and athletic training among undergraduate students. To allow the students various educational and engagement opportunities through seminars provided from various professionals and clinical-based internship opportunities.

name: Sports Medicine Interest Group
description: Our mission is to provide opportunities for medical students to learn about topics and opportunities related to sports medicine, connect with faculty members and other students, and engage in outreach efforts within the greater Cleveland community.

name: Springfest Committee
description: Springfest is a free, annual festival open to all CWRU students. It is planned by the Springfest Committee, a student organization under UPB, and held the weekend before Spring semester finals. Our goal is to create an event where students can relax, de-stress, and have fun before finals. Springfest is an on-campus event featuring food trucks, attractions, student bands and performers, and a national headliner.

name: Sri Lankan Graduate Student Association
description: Pearl is a non-profit, non-sectarian, non-religious student-run organization that strives to introduce and share Sri Lankan cultural heritage with the Case Western Reserve University community and the greater Cleveland community.

name: Staff Advisory Council
description: A. To serve as an advisory group to suggest, comment, and provide feedback on policies and raise awareness of issues that affect the University and the people it serves; B. To establish and maintain a forum for communication between University staff and administration on all levels; C. To establish and maintain a forum for communication among staff at the University.

name: Steel Bridge Team
description: The CWRU Steel Bridge Team designs, fabricates, and builds a 20 foot steel bridge which is tested in a regional competition. Last year, we placed third at the Great Lakes Student Steel Bridge Symposium.

name: Steel Drum Ensemble
description: To provide CWRU students the opportunity to participate in and learn from unique musical experiences with steel drums.

name: Stop The Bleed
description: The mission of Stop The Bleed is to provide training to incoming medical students, physician assistant students, Health Education Center faculty and staff, and members of our Cleveland community. We train individuals on managing life-threatening bleeds outside medical facilities through direct pressure, compression, and tourniquets, increasing our communities readiness to mitigate the number one preventable cause of death - bleeding. Beyond equipping our community members with the necessary skills to save someone's life, our goal as an organization is to disseminate life-saving first-aid suppl

name: Street Law
description: Street Law student volunteers lead an innovative teaching program at the Cuyahoga County Juvenile Court's detention center once a month, offering "know your rights" sessions and interactive lessons for youth ages 14 to 21. The lessons encourage participants to think about the law in a new way and cover relevant legal topics such as discrimination, criminal law, and family law. The program's ultimate goal is to help as many detained youth as possible avoid returning to the juvenile justice system due to a lack of knowledge about the legal process.

name: Student Affairs Development and Learning Committee
description: The Division of Student Affairs Development and Learning Committee provides opportunities for Student Affairs staff to build meaningful connections, continuously develop, and flourish in the work they do.

name: Student Bar Association
description: To secure and promote the free exchange of ideas, inclusiveness, due process, and professional responsibility, and to ensure each and every student's opportunity to participate.

name: Student Centers
description: The Office of Student Centers works to provide a safe, orderly and welcoming environment for the CWRU community to intentionally engage in events and activities that will support student development and enrich the student experience. The Student Centers team oversees the operations and engagement efforts within: Thwing Center, Eldred Hall, The Spot and other designated rooms within Leutner Commons, Carlton Commons, and three outdoor spaces: the Leutner Pavilion, NRV Firepit, and the Southside Lawn.

name: Student Community Outreach Society
description: Our mission is to serve as ambassadors for Case Western Reserve University by fostering strong relationships with alumni, friends, and the broader community, helping to preserve and establish traditions that contribute to the University's advancement. This involves promoting the University's vision through ongoing relationship-building and maintaining connections with its alumni, friends, and community members. Additionally, the aim is to create opportunities for students who demonstrate leadership and a commitment to the University, supporting their development and engagement.

name: Student Dietetic Association
description: SDA is a group for students interested in nutrition and dietetics, including non-nutrition majors. We hold numerous professional development and networking events focusing on current issues in nutrition, as well as career opportunities for those earning a degree in nutrition or nutritional biochemistry. SDA also participates in food and nutrition-related community service events and strives to educate the campus community about healthy living, usually in collaboration with other campus organizations and Bon Appetit. Our group meets twice a month for general body meetings, and holds events thro

name: Student Elections
description: This group serves as a collaborative space for fall and spring student elections. Elections commissioners can contact campusgroups@case.edu for more information.

name: Student Financial Services
description: Student Financial Services is here to provide students with support regarding their SIS student account or CWRU-held student loans at Case Western Reserve University.

name: Student Golfers' Association
description: Hello and welcome to the Student Golf Association (SGA) at Case Western Reserve University! We’re here to make golf fun, accessible, and open to everyone—whether you're a seasoned player or trying it out for the first time. Our focus is on enjoying the game, getting outside, and connecting with others who are curious about golf. We host regular trips to the driving range and organize 9- and 18-hole outings (weather permitting) to make it easy to get involved and improve your skills at your own pace. We’ll keep things going through the winter with indoor and semi-indoor range sessions, so there

name: Student Health Law Association
description: SHLA is dedicated to the professional development of students, faculty, and alumni of the law school in the area of health care law. It is further committed to education, public discourse, and critical analysis of matters related to health care law and policy.

name: Student Intellectual Property Law Association
description: Law students interested in intellectual property as a subject matter, as a future career, or as an expansion on their current practice area gather to learn more about intellectual property, current jurisprudence, and ongoing issues, network with peers and practitioners, and advance the curriculum beyond the classroom.

name: Student Interest Group in Neurology
description: The purpose of SIGN is to introduce medical students to the field of neurology by bringing them together through discussions by neurologists, patient presentations, seminars, journal clubs, and learning materials.

name: Student National Dental Association
description: The Student National Dental Association is an auxiliary of the National Dental Association, founded in 1914, and is the largest and oldest organization of minority oral health professionals in the world. The goal of the SNDA, is to integrate dental students with practicing healthcare practitioners, with the ultimate goal of improving the health manpower distribution among the underserved population as defined by the Department of Health and Human Services. Our mission includes: -Committing to the improvement of the delivery of dental health to all people, with an emphasis on minorities and the

name: Student National Medical/Latino Medical Student Association
description: The SNMA/LMSA Chapter is dedicated to supporting and unifying underrepresented minority medical students, with a focus on Latino, Black and other minority communities. We are committed to promoting the recruitment and retention of Latino and Black medical students at all levels, educating future physicians on health issues affecting underserved populations, and advocating for the rights of minorities in healthcare. Through volunteerism, cultural competency, and social consciousness, we aim to increase the number of clinically excellent and socially responsible physicians who serve underserved

name: Student Organization for Caribbean Ancestry
description: The purpose of SOCA is to create a vibrant and inclusive community that celebrates and promotes Caribbean culture, heritage, and diversity on our campus. We aim to foster a deeper understanding and appreciation of the Caribbean region's rich history, traditions, music, cuisine, and customs. By organizing cultural events, educational initiatives, and social gatherings, we seek to provide a platform for both Caribbean and non-Caribbean students to come together, share experiences, and engage in meaningful dialogue. SOCA is committed to differentiating itself by emphasizing inclusivity, diversity

name: Student Public Interest Law Group
description: The Student Public Interest Law Fellowship (SPILF) at Case Western Reserve University School of Law is a non-profit, non-partisan organization that encourages students to engage in the practice of public interest law in order to correct our legal system's inequities. Public interest areas of law includes assisting the the poor; the un- and under- represented, those deprived of their rights, and the environment. name: Student Sustainability Council
description: The Student Sustainability Council is an ad-hoc council of USG with the purpose of promoting and developing a more sustainable mode of life for students and faculty on CWRU's campus. We aim to create and implement innovative projects dealing with recycling, water conservation, "green" building policies, food waste reduction, and many other topics including educating the student body on environmental issues. name: Students for Rare
description: Students for Rare is a student-led chapter of the National Organization of Rare Disorders (NORD), and is dedicated to promoting research, innovation, awareness, and solidarity around rare diseases on the CWRU campus. Our mission is to engage students in meaningful ways by organizing events that highlight cutting-edge research, support interdisciplinary collaboration, and amplify the voices of those affected by rare diseases. Through awareness campaigns, innovation-focused programming, and patient storytelling events, we aim to create a campus culture that is informed, compassionate, and driven

name: Students for Refugees
description: Students for Refugees (S4R) strives to expand and provide refugee awareness, engagement, and instrumental support. We are committed to empowering both the refugee community and campus community through education and building relationships to create a more inclusive and harmonious world.

name: Students for the Exploration and Development of Space (SEDS)
description: SEDS CWRU exists to promote the exploration and development of space through education, technical project involvement, and professional networking. We provide Case Western Reserve University students with direct access to national competitions, industry conferences, and a broad professional network, empowering a community passionate about space and STEM.

name: Students in Aerospace Medicine
description: To advance the science and art of aerospace and diving medicine among undergraduate, graduate, medical, allied medical and nursing students, as well as among medical residents, throughout the greater campus community.

name: Students Meeting About Risk and Responsibility Training
description: Peer education surrounding Sex, Self, and Substance.
