description: One of the University Media Board's newer organizations, Studio 300 (often stylized "STUDIO300") is a film production club run entirely by CWRU students. We focus on three types of video content: short films, campus life videos, and collaborations with CWRU organizations and/or local groups. Studio 300 was created as a space for students to gain experience with filmmaking in all of its stages -- from brainstorming ideas, to planning the logistics of a shoot, to bringing the script to life behind (or in front of) the camera! Because we aim to provide a hands-on learning experience, students of

name: Study Abroad
description: The Office of Education Abroad supports the mission of CWRU by cultivating a culture of global understanding, responsibility and citizenship through accessible, high-quality courses and learning experiences abroad.

name: Sunrise CWRU
description: Sunrise is a movement to combat the climate crisis and and create a more just & equitable world in the process.

name: Superbugs
description: The purpose of the Council is to serve as a representative body for students in the Case Western Reserve University Superbugs student organization. It aims to build a community for students participating in microbiome related research that will provide opportunities to learn new approaches, share feedback, and establish connections between its members. We will work to foster Superbugs as a friendly environment to discuss microbiome science and foster collaborations between members.

name: Sustainability and Health Student Association
description: Our mission is to promote sustainability in the healthcare field by promoting pre-health students today to be sustainable healthcare workers tomorrow.

name: Sustained Dialogue @ CWRU
description: The mission of the Sustained Dialogue program is to engage members of the CWRU community in dialogues that cultivate strong, trusting relationships and foster respect for each individual and their ability to contribute to positive change.

name: Swetland Center
description: The mission of the Mary Ann Swetland Center for Environmental Health is to study the complex interplay between environmental determinants and population health outcomes. The center places special emphasis on community-engaged approaches that address the role of structural racism in creating and sustaining environmental health inequities. We seek to translate these findings into policies, practices, and relationships that promote community and population health equity.

name: Swing Dance Club
description: The Swing Dancing club of CWRU! We hold free lessons and practice sessions weekly, and attend social dances regularly in the Cleveland dance community. Prior dancing experience is NOT required!

name: Synapse
description: Synapse supports our local community of individuals with brain injuries through cultivating a strong social support network, raising public awareness, and creating a community of advocates.

name: Table Tennis Club
description: The CWRU Table Tennis Club is a proud representative of Case Western Reserve University. We are looking to expand our membership this year, and as we recruit more members we will increase practices and coaching! All members are welcome to our FREE weekly practices, which will be made up of casual meets with singles and doubles, and occasional tournaments throughout the semester. We are also looking for new players to tryout so that we can build a competitive NCTTA team.

name: Tableau User Group
description: TUG is a subgroup within the greater data community at CRWU - Data Users Group (DUG). We are a group of faculty, staff, and students that are passionate about data. We use Tableau, an analytics software platform to analyze, visualize and share data insights. We strive to create an open, engaging community that learns and grows together using Tableau. We have regular meetings where we share tips and tricks, as well as community success stories, which anyone is welcome to attend. No experience in Tableau is necessary to join.

name: Tabletop Empire
description: The Tabletop Empire is CWRU's board game club. We have an expanding library of board, card, and tabletop games that is open to the Case community Saturday afternoons, at Thinkbox 2nd Floor, from 1 - 6 pm. We play all sorts of games, including simple card games like Fluxx, large board games like Cosmic Encounter, and the miniature wargame Warhammer 40k. All players - experienced and new - are welcome!

name: Taekwondo Club
description: Originally founded in 1983, and restarted in 2025, the Case Taekwondo Club is the oldest surviving martial arts club on campus. We are committed to preparing our members for the real world while addressing the morals and philosophy of the art that is Taekwondo. The mission of the Case Western Reserve University Taekwondo Club is two-fold: To provide its members and instructors with the highest possible standards, values, and environment for learning, practicing and instructing the martial arts. name: Taiwanese American Student Association
description: The mission of the Taiwanese American Student Association is to empower and inspire the Taiwanese American community, as well as to work with other cultural groups at Case to promote diversity. By providing events and resources that explore and celebrate Taiwanese American identity, we help develop personal friendships and professional networking.

name: Taiwanese Student Association
description: We are a group of students at Case, CIM, and CIA from Taiwan, who strive to establish an welcoming and comfortable environment through various events, where students may share and experience Taiwanese culture. We provide informational and counseling resources for international students and their families, including academic, cultural, legal, and any other supports as needed. We look forward to build a professional network of Taiwanese students within CWRU and across the greater Cleveland community. Most importantly, we would like to inspire Taiwanese, Taiwanese American, and all other students

name: Tau Beta Pi: Ohio Alpha Chapter
description: An honor society composed of members chosen from eligible students and alumni on the basis of distinguished scholarship or professional attainment and exemplary character in the field of engineering.

description: The Tea & Chocolate Club is a space for graduate and professional students to come together through cultural exchange around tea—the second most consumed beverage in the world after water (Manellis, 2014; Tea Fact Sheet—2019-2020, 2020)—and chocolate. Spaces for graduate students to interact across campus have been limited since COVID-19 started. The T&C Club's purpose is to create such a space for all graduate students while being present through sensory experiences. From answering your questions about technologies, to assistance in developing teaching resources & rethinking your syllabus, to creating active learning environments in face-to-face, blended learning, and online courses, we are eager to help you!

name: Technical Philosophy Club
description: The mission of the Technical Philosophy Club is to foster a community exploring the philosophical dimensions of technology, provide a forum for critical examination of technical systems and paradigms and their societal implications, and promote interdisciplinary dialogue between philosophy, computer science, engineering, and related fields within the university community. For example, we want to host debates on different programming paradigms, ethical considerations with AI, and more.

name: TEDx
description: TEDxCWRU seeks to spread ideas worth sharing from Case Western Reserve University and the Greater Cleveland Community. Fully student run and operated, we host one licensed full-scale TEDx event each academic year with an array of speakers covering a variety disciplines, backgrounds, and modalities. In addition, we host workshops, guest speakers and other activities for students and community members at large throughout the year. name: Tennis Club
description: We work with the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and communicate with other college club tennis teams to arrange tournament opportunities. We offer organized practices to build a community of people of all levels who are passionate about tennis. We hope to unite the tennis players on campus and provide a way for them to regularly play tennis while in college.

name: The Athenian
description: The Athenian first began in the year 2000, started by a couple undergraduates who thought they were funnier than everybody else. Since the early days, The Athenian has grown into a publication featuring satire, comics, anecdotal humor, silly humor, dark humor, irony, self-depreciation, and spelling errors. The Athenian is so named because the Case Western Reserve University mascot is the "Spartans", and thus, being the smart asses we are, we chose the name of one of Sparta's rival cities from back in the day. In doing so, we aim to provide a strong network of support among black males at CWRU. By developing awareness of the issues black men encounter on campus and around the Greater Cleveland Region, we aspire to enhance the black male experience at CWRU.

name: The Film Society
description: The Film Society has been providing the students of CWRU with a place to relax at the end of the week. We show good movies and sell concessions for prices that won't break your bank. Our schedules offer a variety of films through each semester to cater to a broad array of students and community members.

name: The Flea Market
description: CWRU Flea Market is dedicated to empowering our fellow students by offering a dynamic platform that provides the opportunity for students to buy, sell and promote their talents. Our mission is to celebrate and nurture the entrepreneurial spirit within our community while fostering a vibrant atmosphere of creativity and business opportunities. Through the organization of engaging flea market events on campus, we aim to bring together diverse talents, inspire innovation, and create a thriving platform that encourages both personal and collective growth in the realm of entrepreneurship.

name: The Forge
description: The mission of The Forge is to provide students with experiential learning opportunities by applying foundational principles of forging technologies, materials science, mechanical engineering, manufacturing, and design through the conception, analysis, manufacture, testing, and competition of forged products.

name: The Heart Health Collective
description: The Heart Health Collective empowers students to become leaders in heart health through hands-on community impact, education, and wellness promotion. Together, we're building a healthier future one heart at a time,

name: The Hidden Opponent at CWRU

name: The Interreligious Council
description: Our mission is to provide access to programs and services that enable students, faculty, and staff to come together, support one another, and pursue full spiritual growth and development. We work towards facilitating communication, encouraging interreligious dialogue and interaction, and fostering a campus atmosphere in which members of the Case Western Reserve University community may freely express their religion, spirituality, and beliefs.

name: The Letterboxing Club
description: To provide a space for those interested in stamp making and exploring Cleveland through letterboxing.

name: The Mandel School Student-Alumni Network
description: We aim to bridge the gap between students & alumni by facilitating an active relationship through professional development and networking opportunities. We also strive to increase school pride & student awareness of the Mandel School Alumni Board through resources, programming, & special events. Our goal is to enhance the education of students and prepare them to serve as future alumni leaders and volunteers at the Mandel School.

name: The Master Chefs
description: The Master Chefs are dedicated to fostering community bonding and support among its members while making a meaningful impact on the local community through service. We believe in the importance of nutrition—both in preparing and sharing food—as a way for the community to nourish the mind and body. Through collaborative efforts, we aim to empower individuals, promote well-being, and create a supportive environment where members can thrive personally, academically, and professionally.

name: The Steiner House Cooperative

We aim to create a space where students from various cultural, political, racial, religious, national, and socioeconomic backgrounds can come together, learn, and grow. name: The Underrepresented Minority Women in STEM
description: The Underrepresented Minority Women in STEM mission is to provide an empowering network to aid underrepresented minority women to excel in their science, technology, engineering, and mathematics-related courses and future occupations, despite any adversity they may encounter.

name: The Weatherhead Fund
description: The Weatherhead Fund is a student-operated investment club managing a ~$1,400,000 portfolio. All majors and interests are welcome. Industries covered: Consumer & Retail, Diversified Industrials, Financial Institutions & Real Estate (FIGs & REITs), FinTech, Healthcare, and Technology, Media, & Telecom (TMT).

description: The Women's Network (TWN) was created for ambitious women looking to grow professionally while being lifted by their community. TWN offers opportunities to gain exposure to the professional world, network with high-profile speakers and meet peers around their campus and the country. TWN meets biweekly (twice a month) and holds speaker meetings, various networking events, resume, internship and LinkedIn workshops, alumni networking receptions and interactive activity sessions to develop relationships with fellow members. name: Theta Chi
description: Theta Chi Fraternity's mission has been dedicated to developing resolute men. The Fraternity's programs are designed specifically to assist college aged men to become outstanding sons, brothers, fathers, uncles, and models of male behavior in society.

name: Theta Tau
description: Theta Tau is the only professional engineering fraternity on campus. We are a chapter as of November 2016! We have been reinstalled as Delta Chapter of Theta Tau. The three pillars of our organization are brotherhood, service, and professionalism. We are a group of about 80 students from all different disciplines within the Case School or Engineering that help each other navigate through our undergraduate degrees and enter the workforce.

name: Third Culture Association
description: We are a community of Third Culture Kids (TCKs) at CWRU who celebrate our unique journeys, navigate shared challenges, and empower each other to thrive.

name: Three Minute Thesis Competition
description: 3MT competition cultivates students' academic, presentation, and research communication skills. Presenting in a 3MT competition increases their capacity to effectively explain their research in three minutes, in a language appropriate to a non-specialist audience.

name: Thwing Study Over Committee
description: Thwing Study Over is the perfect break from studying as you prepare for finals. Whether you're completing your first year or your fourth year, you won't find a tradition with more food, fun, and friends before final exams than you will here!

name: Tinkham Veale University Center
description: Tinkham Veale University Center fosters inclusivity and is a dynamic space where students, faculty, staff, and the community come together for collaborative ideas.

name: Tsunagari Japan
description: Tsunagari Japan is CWRU's Japanese culture and conversation club. We hold weekly meetings with various cultural activities and provide a space for students to practice their Japanese conversation skills and to learn/experience Japanese culture. We also hold conversation tables throughout the semester for dedicated conversation practice.

name: Turkish Student Association
description: The mission of the Turkish Student Association at Case Western Reserve University is to promote Turkish culture, foster a sense of community among Turkish students, and create an inclusive environment where students can connect, learn, and share cultural experiences. Through cultural events, social gatherings, and educational initiatives, we aim to build cross-cultural understanding and strengthen campus diversity.

name: UCITE

name: UGEN & Executive IT Support

We handle the day-to-day maintenance of computer equipment and provide value-added electronic services for administrative departments outside of the schools. This allows those staff members to spend more of their time providing direct services to students.

name: Ultimate Frisbee Club

The club consists of three teams, Men's Competitive, Women's and Men's Developmental. We practice year round, including a winter season where we practice inside the Veale Fieldhouse. We welcome anyone interested in the sport, experienced player or novice. Anyone and everyone is welcome to come to practice!

name: Undergraduate Advising Support
description: The Undergraduate Advising Support Office provides timely and accurate advice for students on their academic journey through Case Western Reserve University. Four-year advisors connect students to resources of support as needed to allow them to successfully complete their academic degrees.

name: Undergraduate American Medical Women's Association
description: We are dedicated to advancing women in medicine and improving women’s health.

name: Undergraduate Dermatology Society
description: Our mission is to promote awareness and education about skin health while fostering a supportive community for students interested in dermatology. We aim to provide engaging events, hands-on learning opportunities, and meaningful outreach that inspire curiosity, enhance knowledge, and connect members with resources in the field of skin health and dermatologic medicine.

name: Undergraduate Diversity Collaborative
description: The Undergraduate Diversity Collaborative (UDC) is an umbrella organization that aims to support organizations which advocate for the advancement of diversity and inclusion at Case Western Reserve University. The UDC will serve as an advocating body for diversity groups, a platform for voicing student diversity concerns, and a resource for organizations in regards to diversity programming.

name: Undergraduate Human Rights Initiative
description: The Human Rights Initiative's (HRI) primary goal is to assist the CWRU Asylum Clinic, which provides forensic documentation of the physical and psychological sequelae of torture and abuse experienced by individuals applying for asylum in the United States. We also seek to hold advocacy events and increase public awareness for Immigrant and Asylee rights in the United States.

name: Undergraduate Indian Students Association
description: The Undergraduate Indian Students Association (uISA) of Case Western Reserve University is a student-led organization under the Undergraduate Diversity Collaborative (UDC). uISA is one of the largest student organizations on campus as it works independently and in conjunction with other student organizations. Founded by Indian undergraduates, the organization strives to bring awareness of Indian culture and tradition to both Case Western and to the greater Cleveland area. uISA hosts many events throughout the year including celebrations of Navaratri Garba and Diwali. name: Undergraduate Law Journal
description: The CWRU Undergraduate Law Review Journal (CULRJ) aims to produce an entirely student-written and student-run journal of legal scholarship.

name: Undergraduate Materials Society
description: The Undergraduate Materials Society (UMS) is an academic organization created to help students of the Materials Science and Engineering Department and those with interest in materials make the most of their undergraduate experience. To this end, we work together to provide support for students, whether it be i) networking opportunities via meetings of local professional organizations, ii) financially though scholarship applications with local organizations, iii) academically through contacts with professors, or iv) socially in our Lounge.

name: Undergraduate Mock Trial
description: Case's Undergraduate Mock Trial is a competitive organization within the American Mock Trial Association. Students compete as both witnesses and attorneys and present civil and criminal cases in front of attorney evaluators. Mock trial is open to students of all academic disciplines, and no prior experience is required. Anyone interested in gaining confidence, improving public speaking, learning about the law and having fun is encouraged to join! As an organization we have multiple competing teams based on students availability and experience.

name: Undergraduate Psychology Student Organization
description: The purpose of the organization shall be to promote a sense of community among undergraduate students in psychology at Case Western Reserve University and to provide an opportunity to learn more about career paths in psychology and current research within the field.

name: Undergraduate Research Office
description: The Undergraduate Research Office is here to: *help students learn about research and creative project opportunities *assist faculty members with undergraduate research program development and funding *provide educational seminars about the research process and information sessions about our programs *celebrate our students' accomplishments.

name: Undergraduate Research Society
description: Our mission is to utilize the collective experiential knowledge of undergraduate researchers to support one another in their pursuit of research to find research, connect and network, develop skills, develop postgraduate plans, collaboration, and locally impact our society.

name: Undergraduate Society for Bioethics and Health Humanities
description: Undergraduate Society for Bioethics and Health Humanities, a student-run organization, welcomes students from all academic disciplines in order to foster bioethics education outside of the classroom. Bioethics and health humanities are interdisciplinary fields that are engaged in current and cutting-edge ethical issues concerning biomedical research, the delivery of healthcare, and the larger social, cultural, and institutional forces that shape both our shared and individual experiences of health and illness.

name: Undergraduate Student Government
description: #StudentsFirst

name: Undergraduate Student Nurse's Association
description: The USNA strives to advocate for nursing students both on CWRU's campus and across the United States. Everyone enrolled in the Frances Payne Bolton School of Nursing is granted automatic membership to the National Student Nurses Association, but CWRU's USNA board consists of leaders selected by student vote. The Executive Board consists of a President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer, as well as our chapter advisor, Catherine Mohney. name: Undivided
description: The purpose of UNDIVIDED is to provide the students and faculty of Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) with insight into hip-hop culture, to promote school spirit through performances at campus events, and to promote safe and proper dance technique.

name: United World Colleges Network
description: To make education a force to unite people, nations and cultures for peace and a sustainable future" by creating a CWRU and Cleveland community where UWC members are highly valued and influential as leaders in the community.

name: Universal Health Aid at CWRU
description: UHA Cleveland is a non-profit organization that aims to promote a healthy lifestyle to those in the Cleveland community by providing medical resources to those in need, facilitating health education workshops, and promoting collaboration amongst like-minded organizations. In doing so, UHA Cleveland hopes to galvanize students in the effort to alleviate health disparities in the greater Cleveland community.

name: University Center on Aging and Health
description: UCAH's mission is to foster collaboration among its community of scholars, learners, and practitioners in order to encourage and coordinate innovative interdisciplinary research, education, and service programs relevant to the health and well-being of older adults.

name: University Farm
description: The University Farm, which is comprised of Squire Valleevue and Valley Ridge Farms, is a beautiful 400-acre property that features forests, ravines, waterfalls, meadows, ponds, and a self-contained natural watershed. Owned by CWRU, the Farm is the site of several buildings designed for educational, research, and recreational purposes. The Farm is available to all CWRU students, faculty, staff, and alumni. The property and trails are open from dawn to dusk. The goal of the University Farm is to enhance and complement the university's mission of education, research and community service through

name: University Health and Counseling Services
description: The mission of University Health and Counseling Services is to advance the well-being, development, and academic success of our diverse student body through integrated medical, mental health, and wellness services. We collaborate with the entire CWRU community through outreach, education, and services to promote a culture of safety, respect, and global citizenship that fosters lifelong resilience.

name: University Media Board
description: The University Media Board fosters responsible forums of student expression through a variety of media covering writing, photography, cinematography, film, and radio. Groups that fall under the University Media Board fall into the following categories: Print: The Athenian, Discussions, LUX, The Observer, Case Reserve Review, Photography Club Film: Film Society, Studio 300 Radio: WRUW-91.1 FM, W8EDU, CWRU Podcast Theater: CWRU Footlighters, Players' Theater Group, IMPROVment.

name: University Program Board
description: The University Program Board exists to organize, facilitate, and plan programs that support the undergraduate experience and enhance the lives of Case Western Reserve University students by providing educational, social, recreational, and cultural programs that reflect and respond to the wishes of students and the programming needs of the campus. For general questions or if you would like to join, please email upb-exec@case.edu.

name: University Spirit Committee
description: Through collaboration, USC strives to cultivate a strong sense of community among students, faculty, staff, and alumni by promoting Spartan pride and spreading awareness of CWRU's rich history and traditions.

name: University Technology
description: UTech supports and enhances the academic and research mission of CWRU through responsive service, enabling infrastructure, effective administrative systems and innovative solutions.

name: Upperclass Community Council
description: Programming, advocacy, and leadership development in the Upperclass Community

name: Upperclass Experience
description: The Upperclass Experience strives to cultivate an inclusive community optimal for collective growth through support and engagement. Our team connects residents to resources, promotes wellness and prepares residents for life after college.

name: URD National Development
description: This group's purpose is to provide National Development Team staff with departmental resources to support professional success. It will also streamline form submission and approvals.

name: Urology Interest Group
description: The mission of the Urology Interest Group at CWRU SOM is: to provide exposure, professional opportunity, and guidance to students with an interest in the field of urology.

name: Vascular Surgery Interest Group
description: Our mission is to create an environment for medical students to learn about vascular surgery and provide resources to enhance their understanding of this field. Through speaking events, mentorship, and the self-directed surgical skills elective, we hope to support medical students who are pursuing vascular surgery.

name: Veterans Affairs Voluntary Service
description: VAVS shall exist for the benefit of the Louis Stokes Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center and shall augment the voluntary service program there.

name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: The Vietnamese Student Association promotes Vietnamese culture within the diverse Case Western Reserve University campus. We encourage healthy cross cultural relationships and showcase Vietnamese heritage through group activities, events and opportunities. We provide for all students, regardless of their ethnicity, a rich understanding and appreciation of global diversity and Vietnam.

name: VISA Office
description: The mission of the Visa and Immigration Services & Advisors (VISA) Office is to enhance the international experience and promote intercultural exchange at CWRU for students, faculty, staff, scholars, and visitors. This office also works closely with other administrative and academic departments with the following objectives in mind: Provide excellent service to the international students, faculty, staff, scholars, and visitors, as well as to the admissions offices, schools, and academic departments of CWRU. name: Visual Sciences Research Center
description: The mission of the VSRC is to promote the study of basic and clinical problems of the eye and visual system that may lead to improvements in the prevention and treatment of major blinding disorders in the United States and the world.

name: Volleyball Club
description: CWRU Club Volleyball is part of the Club Sports Program that meets 3 times a week in Horsburgh Gym (Veale) to play volleyball. Men and women of all skill levels are welcome to come practice, meet other students, and enjoy the sport of volleyball. We host tournaments for men and women and compete with universities across the country.

name: VTOL CWRU
description: At VTOL CWRU, we are dedicated to pioneering the future of aerial technology through innovation, collaboration, and engineering excellence. Our mission is to compete in the Design-Build-Vertical Flight Competition hosted by the Vertical Flight Society, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in the field of Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) aircraft. name: Warner and Swasey Observatory
description: Founded in 1920, the Warner & Swasey Observatory is the home of CWRU's Rooftop Telescope on AW Smith. We provide training on the telescope and host astronomy-related outreach events on campus.

name: Weatherhead Consulting Club
description: Weatherhead Consulting Club's mission is to empower aspiring consultants by providing exclusive resources, networking opportunities, and career development support. Through access to case study prep material, alumni mentorship, and peer collaboration, we aim to equip our members with the skills and connections needed to succeed in the dynamic world of consulting.

name: Weatherhead Economics Society
description: The Weatherhead Economics Society aims to stimulate and promote student interest in all aspects of economics and to facilitate the development of social bonds between economics students, alumni, faculty, and working professionals. In addition, it provides members with career and networking opportunities and engages with the local community through service projects that are able to benefit from the unique skills of its membership.

name: Weatherhead Finance Club
description: The Finance Club at Weatherhead School of Management is committed to bridging the gap between students and the real world. The club organizes various events that provide students with not only a unique opportunity to learn but also network with alumni, faculty and other students. Club events include an investment banking panel, risk management panel and guest speakers in the industry.

name: Weatherhead Graduate Programs
description: Connect and inform Weatherhead Graduate Students in the Full-Time MBA & Specialty Programs about events, academic reminders, job postings, and more.

name: Weatherhead Graduate Student Experience
description: The Weatherhead Graduate Student Experience Office integrates the rigors of the academic classroom with opportunities to develop and practice the social, organizational, creative and professional skills that help the bright candidate shine even brighter in the candidate pool and in the workplace. Weatherhead student experience offers over a dozen graduate student organizations and clubs, as well as opportunities throughout the year to hear from and connect with local, regional and national business leaders on topics that will help students further develop into transformational leaders.

name: Weatherhead Healthcare Club
description: The Weatherhead Healthcare Club (WHC) at Case Western Reserve University Weatherhead School of Management provides a professional network and extracurricular education for students interested in the business of healthcare delivery. Whether students are interested in the fields of hospital administration, payment reform, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, consulting, or continuing education in the field of medicine; WHC will prepare members for successful recruiting in healthcare-related firms.

name: Weatherhead Master of Finance Program
description: Connect and inform the Weatherhead Master of Finance program about events, academic reminders, job postings, and more.

name: Weatherhead Multicultural Club
description: Multicultural Club aims to create a sense of belonging by celebrating diversity of culture among students, faculty, and staff. This organization aims to: promote awareness, acceptance, and appreciation of diverse cultures; have some fun and meet new friends; do a variety of activities comprised of games and events; and bring students together in a friendly, celebratory, and educative manner.

name: Weatherhead Undergraduate Programs
description: Weatherhead Undergraduate Programs is an academic affairs and student services office that provides academic advising for Accounting, Economics, and Management majors and minors, as well as faculty support and program administration. We work closely with Admissions, the University Career Center, the Office of Undergraduate Studies, Orientation, University Office of Student Affairs, and others in an effort to outreach and communicate with prospective and current students, alumni, and employers.

name: Weatherhead Women in Business
description: Weatherhead Women in Business seek to inspire, connect and innovate. We are tirelessly aiming to increase awareness of gender issues in the workplace and to inspire our female student body to realize that there are many resources at their fingertips to help them achieve their goals. We are always looking to connect students to successful female professionals across all industries and fields who can share their experiences and advice in and out of the workplace. name: Wilderness Medicine Interest Group
description: The Wilderness Medicine Interest Group exists to promote knowledge and skill development in the field of wilderness medicine and to help foster and sustain love for wild spaces. We coordinate group outings and skills workshops and serve as a repository of knowledge and experience for those looking to increase their comfort in the outdoors.

name: Women Faculty of the School of Medicine
description: The mission of the Women Faculty of the School of Medicine is to ensure all individuals have a strong foundation to succeed in academic medicine by providing professional development opportunities, advocacy for issues that disproportionately impact women faculty in academic medicine, and networking among faculty and leaders in academic medicine to promote academic, professional, and personal growth for all. This group is open to all.

name: Women in Data Science
description: Our focus is on fostering learning through collaborative group projects and engaging in data-thons. This club will not only serve as an incredible networking platform, but it will also be a dynamic space for women and non binary students aspiring to major in or learn more about data science data science. Beyond that, the club provides a gateway to a broader network of women in the field through the international Women in Data Science (WIDS) program.

name: Women In Dentistry Club
description: Women in Dentistry is a student-run organization that aids CWRU SODM students in the empowerment of women in the field of dentistry through professional development, service, scholarship, and friendship. Women in Dentistry introduces students to valuable education, experiences, and networking that will help them construct an impactful career as an empowered provider true to gender equality and female empowerment.

name: Women in Economics
description: Women in Economics is an organization that support women as well as other underrepresented minority students in economics through community, mentorship, speakers, and collaboration with other groups hosting events. WE is interested in increasing representation of women and minorities in all levels of economics, from college majors to careers in economics.

name: Women in Finance
description: The goal of Women in Finance is to increase the advancement of women in Banking and Finance careers and contribute to the development of a more meritocratic and diverse banking and finance workforce of the future.

name: Women in Orthopedics
description: The mission of the Women in Orthopedics (WIO) is to promote the professional development of women in orthopaedics throughout all stages of their careers. WIO welcomes members of all genders to join our growing club. WIO offers a variety of benefits and opportunities to its members, including leadership courses to enhance leadership skills, scholarship and grant opportunities to support residents and medical students, networking with members at all levels, access to professional development resources, mentorship programs for both mentoring and being mentored. name: Women in Science and Engineering Roundtable
description: WISER (Women in Science and Engineering Roundtable) is open to CWRU students (undergraduate, graduate and professional) majoring in or planning a career in science, technology, engineering, medicine or math. Our mission is to promote the inclusion and success of all women pursuing a STEM-related career at Case Western Reserve University through leadership, mentorship, and outreach. New members, guests, and CWRU faculty and staff are always welcome to all WISER events. name: Women In Science and Humanities Earning Doctorates
description: To create a community of woman-identifying doctoral students and candidates with the goals of providing social and professional resources, and tools for individual and collective development.

name: Women's Club Basketball
description: Our group's mission is to provide female students of CWRU with an inclusive and exciting environment in which to play and enjoy basketball competitively.

name: Women's Law Association
description: To create a social, professional, and academic community at CWRU law school for women law. • To empower women in law school and in the legal profession through social, professional, and academic networking. • To educate the community at large about the unique legal issues women of all ages, in all professions, and from all backgrounds face. • To advance the legal profession by promoting women's issues to create a better profession for both men and women. name: Wood Craft Club
description: The purpose of the Wood Craft Club is to foster a community of woodworking enthusiasts who are passionate about the craft of working with wood. We aim to provide a supportive and resource-rich environment where members of all skill levels—from beginners to advanced craftsmen—can explore their creativity, develop their woodworking skills, and share their knowledge and experiences. Our club is dedicated to promoting the appreciation of woodcraft as an art form and a practical skill, encouraging sustainable practices, and contributing to the preservation of traditional woodworking techniques.

name: Writers In Residence
description: Teach creative writing to incarcerated youth.

name: Writers Writing Words
description: Writers Writing Words is a club for anyone who enjoys creative writing. Whether it's poetry, short stories, songs, or that one novel everyone has been secretly working on since middle school, all are welcome. We meet from 2:00 to 3:00 every Saturday on in Clark Hall 309. If you're interested, feel free to stop by anytime! In our meetings, we host writing workshops to develop a specific aspect of creative writing, from worldbuilding to speed writing to developing dialogue. name: WRUW FM
description: More Music, Fewer Hits

name: Yarn Arts Club
description: Our mission is to teach and practice the yarn arts and to help the community through the donation of hand-made products.

name: Yoga Club
description: To provide free, quality yoga classes to CWRU community members.

name: Yoga Interest Group
description: The mission of the CWRU SOM Yoga Interest Group is to promote wellness, resilience, and mindfulness among medical students by fostering a deeper connection between the body and mind. Through yoga, meditation, breathing exercises, and other evidence-based relaxation practices taught by medical students certified in yoga instruction, the club provides students with a supportive environment to reduce stress, improve mental and physical well-being, and cultivate healthy coping strategies. name: Youth Programs
description: Youth programs and activities at Case Western Reserve University are consistent with the university's mission; they promote education generally and benefit many children and teens by providing enriching experiences.

name: Zeta Beta Tau
description: The mission of Zeta Beta Tau Fraternity (ZBT) is to foster and develop in its brotherhood the tenets of its Credo: Intellectual Awareness, Social Responsibility, Integrity and Brotherly Love, in order to prepare its brothers for positions of leadership and service within their communities.
